findings.title: mergePolicy does not handle conflicting skip reasons across chunks
findings.detail: The mergePolicy function picks the first reason seen for an agent when multiple chunks report skips with different reasons. This conflict resolution is not tested.
findings.evidence: // The merge keeps `agentsSkipped` for agents skipped in **every** chunk, and demotes a partial skip to the narrowed-diff note...
findings.impact: When an agent is skipped in multiple chunks with different exclusion reasons, the rendered report will show only the first reason, potentially hiding important context about other exclusion causes.

findings.title: Unnecessary Map allocation in mergePolicy hot path
findings.detail: mergePolicy creates new Map<AgentName,number> for each chunk run, then reads repeatedly. For high-chunk-count scenarios this adds O(n) allocations per merge call.
findings.suggestion: Use object instead of Map for string-keyed aggregation when order doesn't matter

findings.title: Array deduplication + sort in mergeFilteredFiles creates new arrays each iteration
findings.detail: mergeFilteredFiles creates a new array and sorts it for every agent per chunk, causing O(n*m log m) where n=chunks, m=files. For large diffs with many files this becomes expensive.
findings.suggestion: Accumulate with Map and sort once at the end rather than sorting per iteration

findings.title: Empty filteredFiles object causes false undefined comparison
findings.detail: When result.filteredFiles exists but is an empty object {}, Object.keys().length returns 0, but the filter condition allows it through. An attacker could send an empty filteredFiles object that would cause mergedFilteredFiles to incorrectly return undefined when files were actually filtered.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit null/undefined check and length guard: "if (result.filteredFiles && typeof result.filteredFiles === 'object' && !Array.isArray(result.filteredFiles) && Object.keys(result.filteredFiles).length > 0)"
findings.suggestion: Add explicit null/undefined check and length guard: "if (result.filteredFiles && typeof result.filteredFiles === 'object' && !Array.isArray(result.filteredFiles) && Object.keys(result.filteredFiles).length > 0)"

findings.title: mergeResults has CCN of 22 - high cyclomatic complexity
findings.detail: The mergeResults function exhibits excessive cyclomatic complexity (22 decision paths) for a file-merging operation. The function merges multiple result fields using different strategies per-field, with complex branching logic that makes reasoning about field propagation difficult. This complexity increases debugging difficulty and testing surface.
findings.evidence: CCN=22 for mergeResults@127-243 (from lizard metrics). The function handles: last-chunk-wins vs merged policies, filteredFiles unions, agentStatus merging, toolAvailability collapsing to 'partial', etc.
findings.recommendation: Extract each field's merge strategy into separate helper functions. Create a config object describing merge rules per-field.
findings.suggestion: Decompose the multi-strategy merge logic into individual merge* helpers with clear naming

findings.title: formatMcpOutput has CCN of 26 - high cyclomatic complexity
findings.detail: formatMcpOutput exhibits high cyclomatic complexity (26 decision paths) for formatting MCP output. The function now handles multiple policy states: normal results, agent skips, narrowed views, degraded tools. This complexity makes it harder to maintain consistent formatting across all code paths and increases cognitive load for reviewers.
findings.evidence: CCN=26 for formatMcpOutput@20-190 (from lizard metrics). The function now checks earlyExit, agentsSkipped, narrowed agents, toolAvailability with degraded states, and more.
findings.recommendation: Extract policy-related formatting into separate functions. Create a dedicated policyNotes helper that returns string arrays for different states.
findings.suggestion: Extract policy-related formatting into separate functions. Create a dedicated policyNotes helper that returns string arrays for different states.
